title: Soundness of the successor reader
statement: For every bound $n\in\mathbb N$, bit string $x$, optional state $s\in\{	ext{none}\}\cup\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and suffix $r$, if the successor-state reader with bound $n$ applied to $x$ returns $s$ and $r$, then $x$ is the encoding of $s$ followed by $r$. The encoding is $0$ for no state and, for state $i$, a $1$ followed by $i$ ones and a $0$.
hypotheses_covered: An optional state s in Fin n
The successor-state reader succeeds on x and returns (s,r)
replaced:
If the successor-state reader with bound $n$ succeeds on a bit string $x$,
returning a field $s$ and a suffix $r$, then $x$ is exactly the encoding of $s$
(a single $0$ for halt, or a $1$ followed by the unary code of a live state
below $n$) followed by $r$.
